title: Teensy 4.1 USB REPL output hangs after several seconds of inactivity
body: On my Teensy 4.1, MicroPython hangs while running simple_benchmarks.py. I reduced it to a short script where adding time.sleep(0.1) causes the final print to hang, while printing a dot during each iteration lets it finish. I am using MicroPython v1.19.1-782-g699477d12 on a Teensy 4.1 with MIMXRT1062DVJ6A. A still smaller reproduction is print('Start..'), time.sleep(5), print('Finish'): after more than about four seconds, the final print hangs.

symptoms_visible: On my Teensy 4.1, print('Start..'), a five-second delay, and print('Finish') displays the first text but not the final text.
Printing a dot at intervals lets the longer benchmark run through normally.
N0.label: N0 delayed USB output hang reported

symptoms_visible: With an LED around the delay, the LED turns on and then turns off after five seconds, but USB does not display 'Finish' or return normally to the REPL.
The same behavior occurs in screen instead of Thonny, and Ctrl-D still causes a soft reboot.
CircuitPython on the same Teensy completes both the two-second and five-second tests.
N1.label: N1 program completion separated from USB output

symptoms_visible: When USB and UART REPL channels are active together, the five-second test prints 'Finish' and returns to the prompt on UART, while the USB terminal remains stalled.
Pressing Enter in the stalled USB terminal can bring back a prompt without the missing 'Finish' output.
N2.label: N2 UART comparison isolates USB channel

symptoms_visible: The five-second test and the benchmark complete normally with the Teensy connected to a Windows 10 laptop.
On my NUC running Manjaro Linux, USB output still stalls after the idle interval.
N3.label: N3 behavior differs by host computer

symptoms_visible: After I disabled USB autosuspend on my Manjaro system, the five-second test and USB REPL output worked normally and the problem was gone.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved by disabling host USB autosuspend

question_patterns: Can you toggle an LED around the delay so we can tell whether execution stops or only the output stops?
Please use an LED or another side effect to show whether the program continues past the five-second wait.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I put an LED around the delay. The two-second test works. In the five-second test the LED turns on and switches off after five seconds, but 'Finish' is not printed. Ctrl-D still causes a soft reboot.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The LED stays on permanently, so execution never gets past the delay.
The LED switches off after six seconds instead of five, but the final USB output is still missing.

edges.comment: Reporter evidence from c3-c4: the requested LED probe shows that the five-second operation completes even though USB output and the normal REPL return are absent. The reporter also reproduced it with screen rather than Thonny and later reported CircuitPython behavior on the same Teensy in c9.

question_patterns: Can you expose the REPL on UART as well and compare what appears on UART and USB during the same test?
Please run the delayed test with a serial REPL channel active and report whether the final output appears there.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I enabled a UART REPL with os.dupterm(uart). The two-second test passes on both channels. With the five-second test, 'Finish' and the REPL prompt appear on the serial line, but USB stalls. Pressing Enter on USB can return a prompt without showing 'Finish'.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Neither UART nor USB prints 'Finish', and neither channel returns to the REPL.
UART prints 'Finish' a fraction of a second before USB, but both channels return normally.

edges.comment: Reporter measurements from c21 and c23: on the reporter's Teensy, the same execution produces final output on UART while USB remains stalled. This is the opening reporter's system, not participant1's separate MIMXRT1050 memory-allocation reproducer.

question_patterns: Which operating system is the affected computer using, and can you repeat the same test on another computer?
Does the behavior follow the Teensy when you connect it to a different host machine?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: My affected NUC runs Manjaro Linux. I tried the same Teensy on my son's Windows 10 laptop and test5() had no problem there. The full simple_benchmarks.py test also ran to completion on Windows 10.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The same Teensy stalls in exactly the same way on Manjaro, Windows 10, and another Linux computer.
It works on a second Linux computer as well as on Windows, but still fails on my Manjaro NUC.
The Windows laptop uses a different terminal font and keyboard layout.

edges.comment: Reporter evidence from c26-c27: the delayed test and benchmark work with the same board on the reporter's son's Windows 10 laptop but fail on the reporter's Manjaro NUC. This host comparison is distinct from participant1's unrelated dynamic-memory crashes.

solution.intent: Treat the stall as host-side USB power management after the execution, UART, and cross-host tests; disable USB autosuspend on the affected Manjaro system and rerun the delayed USB test.
solution.concrete_example: Disable USB autosuspend at boot on the affected Manjaro PC using the distribution's USB power-management guidance, reconnect the Teensy, and rerun test5() and the benchmark over USB.
solution.inference_hint: The LED proves execution reaches the end, UART receives the missing output while USB does not, and the same board works on another host. Together these observations point away from a VM or benchmark crash and toward host-side USB inactivity handling. The reporter then confirmed the specific cause by disabling USB autosuspend and observing that the problem disappeared.

edges.comment: Accepted resolution from c32-c34, on the opening reporter's Manjaro PCs: participant1 asked about host power saving, and the reporter disabled USB autosuspend and confirmed the problem was gone. Later TinyUSB callback and descriptor speculation did not replace this accepted diagnosis.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause as USB autosuspend on the reporter's Manjaro host, rather than a MicroPython VM hang, float-allocation failure, or the separate dynamic-memory crash discussed by another participant.
Must ground the diagnosis in the collected evidence: the LED shows execution completes, the final output appears on UART while USB stalls, and the same Teensy and tests work on a Windows 10 host.
Must recommend disabling USB autosuspend on the affected host and then rerunning the same delayed USB test or benchmark.
Must not present garbage collection, a DEBUG firmware, periodic print output, or empty TinyUSB suspend callbacks as the actual fix.
Must treat the issue as resolved only after the reporter verifies that USB output works normally with autosuspend disabled.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable embedded-device user who can flash alternate firmware, wire a UART adapter, configure os.dupterm, compare implementations, and run controlled timing and LED probes, but asks maintainers for guidance on firmware internals and debugging.
persona_hint.communication_style: Persistent, investigative, and cooperative; supplies reduced reproductions and detailed observations, challenges competing explanations when evidence suggests separate issues, and follows up with confirmation when a host configuration change resolves the problem.
